newsitem.title: BRAZIL: POLL - Brazil unlikely to have sharp devaluation.
newsitem.headline: POLL - Brazil unlikely to have sharp devaluation.

text.p: Brazil will probably avoid a sharp devaluation in the next few years, but if one were to come it would happen after the October 1998 presidential election, according to a Reuters poll of Brazilian and U.S. banks.
The survey of 40 banks, brokerages and research houses found that the greatest probability of an overnight, 15-20 percent devaluation of Brazil's real was 24 percent in first half 1999.
That was followed by a 21 percent chance in second half 1999 and an 18 percent chance in first half of 2000.
Devaluation risk fell dramatically in semesters before the election, with banks on average saying there was just a 3 percent chance in the current semester and a 4 percent chance in first half 1998.
In second half 1998, when the election will take place, the chance rose to 10 percent.

Four of the participants, or 10 percent, said the risk of an overnight devaluation was zero in every semester. Some 20 percent of respondents, however, said the chance of devaluation was 50 percent or higher in first half 1999.
The highest probability of devaluation given by any participant in any semester was an 80 percent chance in the second half of 1998. One respondent gave that result.

Reuters surveyed economists based in Sao Paulo, Rio de Janeiro and New York from Aug 11-13, asking them to rate the probability of an overnight, 15-20 percent devaluation in six-months period between H2 1997 and H1 2000.

They were asked to limit their responses to numbers ending in 0, for example O percent, 10 percent, 20 percent, 100 percent. Q. What are the percentage chances of a 15-20 percent devaluation in Brazil?

Participants: BBA-Creditanstalt; Banco BMC; Banco de Boston; Banco Fator; Banco Graphus; Banco Indosuez; Banco Omega; Banco Patrimonio; Banco Pontual; Banco Primus; Banco Sudameris; Bankers Trust; Bicbanco; Bozano, Simonsen; Bradesco; Chase Manhattan; Citibank; Caspian Securities; Credit Lyonnais; CS First Boston; Deutsche-Morgan Grenfell; Fonte-Cindam; Hedging-Griffo; IDEA; ING Barings; Lloyds Bank; MCM Consultores; Marka; Matrix; Morgan Stanley Dean Whitter; Nomura; Paribas; SBC Warbrug; Santander; Schahin Cury; Robert Fleming; Tendencia; Trend; UBS; Unibanco.
